introduction_section.heading: What is Enterprise-Grade
content: Enterprise-grade wireframing defines the structure, layout, screen hierarchy, user flow, and core functionality of a digital product before high-cost development begins. It gives teams a clear blueprint for how a web app, mobile app, SaaS platform, dashboard, portal, or marketplace should work.

Prototyping turns those wireframes into an interactive experience that stakeholders and users can click through. At Devisgon, we create low-fidelity wireframes, high-fidelity prototypes, user flow diagrams, interaction models, usability test plans, and developer-ready handoff files.
This process helps product teams test logic, validate user journeys, identify usability problems, refine MVP scope, and reduce expensive development rework before the engineering phase starts.
introduction_section.highlight_quote: “Wireframes reduce ambiguity, and prototypes reveal product problems before they become expensive development mistakes.”

faq_section.title: Prototyping & Wireframing Questions and Answers
faq_section.subtitle: Detailed answers for founders, startups, product teams, SaaS companies, and businesses validating software ideas

questions.question: What is the difference between wireframing and prototyping?
questions.answer: Wireframing defines the structure, layout, hierarchy, and content placement of screens. Prototyping adds interaction so users and stakeholders can click through the product flow before development. Wireframes show what needs to exist, while prototypes show how the experience should work.

questions.question: Why should we prototype before coding?
questions.answer: Prototyping helps teams find unclear flows, missing screens, usability problems, and weak product logic before development costs increase. It gives founders, designers, developers, and stakeholders a shared reference. Fixing problems in a prototype is faster and cheaper than rebuilding finished code.

questions.question: Can a prototype be used for investor presentations?
questions.answer: Yes. A clickable prototype can help investors understand the product vision, user journey, interface, and core value without requiring a fully built backend. It is especially useful for early-stage startups that need to demonstrate product direction before funding or full development.

questions.question: What is a low-fidelity wireframe?
questions.answer: A low-fidelity wireframe is a simple grayscale layout focused on structure instead of final visuals. It helps define screen sections, user actions, content hierarchy, and navigation before branding and detailed UI design are applied. It is useful for fast exploration and early feedback.

questions.question: What is a high-fidelity prototype?
questions.answer: A high-fidelity prototype looks close to the final product and includes polished UI, realistic content, brand styling, clickable interactions, and simulated flows. It helps stakeholders test the experience, validate user journeys, and prepare a clearer handoff for development.

questions.question: Does a prototype use real backend data?
questions.answer: Most prototypes use simulated data and clickable interactions instead of live databases or APIs. The goal is to validate product logic, usability, and interface flow before backend development. Real data integration usually happens during the engineering phase.

questions.question: Can Devisgon create prototypes for mobile apps and SaaS platforms?
questions.answer: Yes. Devisgon creates wireframes and prototypes for mobile apps, SaaS platforms, web applications, dashboards, marketplaces, portals, internal tools, and MVPs. We design the prototype around your users, product goals, technical scope, and validation needs.

questions.question: Do you provide developer-ready handoff after prototyping?
questions.answer: Yes. We provide organized design files, screen flows, annotations, assets, interaction notes, and implementation guidance so developers understand what to build. A strong handoff reduces confusion and helps development move faster with fewer revisions.
